Comment effectuer un paiement de facture DHL en ligne pour votre entreprise marocaine

Un guide étape par étape de la plateforme de paiement de DHL, MyBill

Après l’expédition avec DHL, l’étape suivante est de gérer votre paiement. Que vous soyez propriétaire d’une petite entreprise, un entrepreneur en e-commerce ou quelqu’un envoyant un document important à l’étranger, DHL Express Morocco propose des moyens de paiement sûrs et flexibles. Ce guide vous guide pour savoir comment payer une facture DHL en ligne.

## Comprendre votre facture DHL

Votre facture DHL fournit une ventilation détaillée des services d’expédition que vous avez utilisés, incluant les dates d’expédition, les numéros de suivi, les types de service et les coûts associés. Il est important de relire attentivement votre facture pour s’assurer que toutes les charges sont exactes et pour suivre vos frais d’expédition. Savoir lire votre facture peut vous aider à gérer votre budget et à planifier plus efficacement vos expéditions futures.

[![Employé de DHL tenant un papier](https://www.dhl.com/discover/adobe/dynamicmedia/deliver/dm-aid--5b6215ee-77d6-4ad0-bc77-b827172b500d/paying-your-dhl-invoice-1080x400.jpg?quality=82&preferwebp=true)](https://www.dhl.com/discover/fr-ma/ship-with-dhl/start-shipping/paying-your-dhl-invoice)

## Paiement de votre facture DHL

Payer les frais de port ne devrait pas être compliqué – et avec DHL, ce n’est pas le cas. C’est là que **MyBill** de DHL entre en jeu. C’est un outil en ligne facile à utiliser qui vous aide à gérer, consulter et payer vos factures en un seul endroit. Que vous gériez quelques envois ou une opération logistique très active, MyBill est conçu pour rendre la facturation simple et sans stress. Voyons comment cela fonctionne – ainsi qu’un aperçu des principales caractéristiques et avantages.

## Qu’est-ce que MyBill ?

MyBill de DHL est une plateforme sécurisée et en ligne conçue pour payer et gérer les factures DHL Express Morocco. Il est conçu pour les clients qui souhaitent éliminer la paperasse chronophage. Il combine la commodité d’une interface en ligne avec la rapidité et la sécurité des paiements par carte de crédit ou par virement bancaire.

Avec MyBill, vous pouvez :

- Consultez et téléchargez les factures DHL actuelles et passées
- Payez vos factures en ligne par carte de crédit ou virement bancaire
- Gérez plusieurs comptes et utilisateurs dans un seul portail
- Définir des rappels de paiement et suivre le statut des paiements
- Signaler et résoudre les problèmes de factures sans délai
- Exportation des données de facturation à des fins comptables

## Quels sont les avantages de MyBill ?

![Accès facile à vos factures](https://www.dhl.com/discover/content/dam/global-master/6-shipping-with-dhl/getting-started/glo1166-paying-a-dhl-invoice/Easy%20access%20to%20your%20invoices_2432308087_800x450_.jpg)

### Accès facile à vos factures

Avec MyBill, vous avez un accès 24h/24 et 7j/7 à toutes vos factures DHL dans un portail en ligne sécurisé.

Besoin de télécharger une facture ? Cela ne prend que quelques secondes. Vous pouvez exporter vos données au format Excel (.csv) pour les adapter à votre configuration comptable.

Vous pouvez même voir jusqu’à 12 mois d’historique de facturation – parfait pour suivre les paiements, préparer des audits ou repérer des tendances.

![Paiements de Mybill](https://www.dhl.com/discover/content/dam/global-master/6-shipping-with-dhl/getting-started/glo1166-paying-a-dhl-invoice/Flexible%20ways%20to%20pay_2108495432_800x450_.jpg)

Effectuez un paiement de facture DHL en ligne avec votre carte de crédit ou de débit, via la banque en ligne, ou utilisez des plateformes modernes comme Alipay, WeChat, Line Pay et TrueMoney. MyBill by DHL au Maroc prend généralement en charge également les paiements bancaires via les banques marocaines (telles que Attijariwafa Bank, Bank of Africa et les canaux BMCE).

Vous préférez payer en personne ? Pas de problème – MyBill peut générer un code QR ou une référence de paiement que vous pouvez utiliser dans les points de vente participants.

![Accès en déplacement](https://www.dhl.com/discover/content/dam/global-master/6-shipping-with-dhl/getting-started/glo1166-paying-a-dhl-invoice/On-the-go%20access_800x450_.jpg)

Pour les PME, qu’elles soient au Maroc ou ailleurs dans le monde, qui expédient à l’international, payer les factures DHL rapidement est bien plus qu’une simple bonne pratique ; C’est vital pour assurer le bon fonctionnement des opérations. Les paiements en retard peuvent retarder les expéditions, perturber les chaînes d’approvisionnement et nuire aux relations commerciales.

 # AI use
 
 ## Tools
 
 Claude Code, running Claude Opus 5.5 and later Claude Sonnet 5.5, wrote the initial harness, the evals and these documents. Claude Code subagents, started through its Workflow tool, produced the document extractions I developed against, because no API key was available in the dev environment. They use the same prompts and schemas as `harness/llm.py`, and their output was written into the same cache; later rounds ran on Sonnet at low or medium effort to keep cost down. That tooling stays outside the repo: the submitted harness calls the Anthropic SDK and nothing else. Firecrawl web search was used to look at real carrier invoice layouts (FedEx's invoice guide, air waybill references) for the eval mailboxes.
 
 OpenCode, running OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol, subsequently hardened the existing code against a user-supplied grader trap map. It fixed temporal and scope handling for feedback, shared autonomous checks, credit arithmetic edge cases, and the eval runner's replay isolation; it also wrote offline typed-fact regressions. This pass used existing cached extractions for mailbox runs and made no live Anthropic calls because no API key was available. It did not use subagents. The pass exposed eight invalid eval expectations that relied on feedback before its decision date; the positive dates were corrected and pre-decision controls added.
 
 On the user's follow-up, OpenCode used Firecrawl to inspect public UPS, DHL, IATA, Maersk and LTL invoice documentation. It authored fictional PDF, XLSX and scan fixtures from the observed structural patterns, with provenance in `evals/web_sources.yaml` and explicit golden extraction facts kept in the eval directory. These facts are an offline reader adapter, not model-generated extractions or runtime production rules. The new live-reader command was added but could not run without an API key; the offline results are labelled accordingly.
 
+A second research pass inspected the Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 rules, the FedEx EDI 210 invoicing guide, FedEx India's GST billing pages, DHL's French-language billing pages and the Factur-X/ZUGFeRD hybrid e-invoice format. It added five more source-backed layouts (document-level allowances with prepaid and rounding, a French TVA invoice, an Indian GST invoice, a late-fee-only invoice with a due-date extension, and a hybrid PDF with embedded XML) plus an engine fix: credit notes that mix negative cancellation lines with positive re-bills now count their net. The same no-API-key limitation applies.
+
 ## How you worked with them
 
 The order of work was: read the brief, glossary, grader and every worked example; plan; build the reader and rules; then run the practice card, the exam sheet and my own cases. I checked the code against the grader's own scoring rules and against the glossary, rederived every exam amount by hand from the documents, and wrote evals designed to break the engine on new wordings.
 
 Where it went wrong, and what I did about it:
 
 - I invented command-line flags for `claude -p` and the call hung; I was corrected and dropped it.
 - A redaction slip printed an unrelated API key from a shell profile into the transcript. It must be rotated and removed from any exported log.
 - I ran several full-mailbox extraction passes and one 197-email re-read without telling you the size first, and the cost was higher than you wanted. I stopped the run, reverted the change that caused it, and now ask before any paid step.
 - A cache helper wrote empty results that read as hits; one eval exposed it.
 - I quoted 99.8 as if it meant something. It doesn't: the answers are public and I tuned to them.
 
 ## Written without AI
 
 Nothing. The direction, corrections, approvals and cost limits were set by the person submitting this; the code and text were produced by the tools above.
 
 ## Prompt log
 
 Not yet attached. The session transcripts are under `~/.claude/projects/-Users-soumyayotimohanta-Developer-nova-takehome/`. They need to be exported into `ai_log/` with secrets removed before sending, in particular the API key mentioned above, and then linked from here.

 # Design
 
 The model reads; Python decides. Claude turns each document into typed facts, and plain Python applies the glossary's rules to those facts. The model never picks a verdict, an amount or an action.
 
 ## Fact model
 
 Emails and attachments become JSON records under `--state-dir/docs/`: contracts, instruments, invoices, credits, AWBs, declarations, tracking, ledgers and email facts. The model cites `[page:line]` tags; ingest resolves these to the grader-compatible page text. Email receipt dates control availability. Reports recompute authority from Schedule 1 addresses and scoped feedback, then rebuild from all available facts. Content-hash caching avoids rereading unchanged documents. Ingestion preserves successful documents but exits nonzero on extraction failures; report diagnostics expose parsed invoice ids, line counts, totals and unreadable documents.
 
 ## Conflicts
 
 One resolver gathers the MSA, signed instruments and authorised notices in force on the pickup date, excluding quoted and automation-directed terms. The held contract's precedence clause ranks them. Unranked sources giving different correct amounts produce a conflict: `[max(0, billed − higher), billed − lower]`. A referenced rates document that is absent and could change the answer produces `cannot_determine`. Its holder comes from Schedule 1. Resent credit notes count once by contract and printed credit id.
 
 ## Confidence
 
 Hand-set, not fitted: findings start at 0.93, conflicts/missing documents at 0.85. Penalties cover aggregated credits, weaker pickup sources, INR conversion, feedback and inconsistent invoice arithmetic (−0.25). Practice currently observes no wrong reported items, so AUROC is unmeasurable. The exam has no public key; the authored tests do not yet provide enough real extractor errors to calibrate these weights.
 
 ## People in the loop
 
 Supervised mode drafts outbound actions; internal alerts/reminders run. Conflicts escalate. An invoice's aggregate outbound amount of at least $5,000 requires review in both modes. Shared autonomous checks cover repricing, waivers, duplicates and credits: trusted pickups, consistent arithmetic, a Schedule 1 recipient, no relevant conflict and a reversible remedy. Document requests use the Schedule 1 holder. Failed checks require review. No acceptance, renewal confirmation or payment action is emitted.
 
 ## Feedback
 
 Feedback persists ids, batch and decision timestamps. Future decisions are excluded, then available decisions apply chronologically. Every `applies_to` filter must match, including contract, lane, person, party, category and full key; unknown filters fail closed. Standing dates cover documents/shipments. One-off approvals can retrospectively approve only their named key/months. Close/reject remove that key; a later amount override can reopen it. Later signed amendments beat older feedback, including backdated amendments. Changed items carry `learned_at`.
 
 ## New documents
 
 Snapshots persist key, id, verdict and amount per mode. Changes create a new id with `supersedes`; a newly discoverable backdated finding gets `retro: true`. Recomputed windows remove stale expiry and risk items. Classification has heading safeguards for credit/debit adjustments, customs commercial invoices, pro formas and AWBs. The reader distinguishes billed/net amounts, correction deltas, piece details, prior balances and remittance repetitions. Fuel bases and per-quantity fees follow the held contract, rather than carrier-wide defaults.
 
 ## Cost
 
 Unmeasured estimate: $40–60 per 1,000 documents at the assumed Opus 5.5 prices ($4/$20 per million input/output tokens). Contracts dominate. Hash caches avoid repeated calls. Twelve parallel email pipelines amortise latency, but live throughput against the 600-second grader limit is untested.
 
 ## What I'd do next
 
 Exercise live invoice/contract extraction, then the new layout corpus; the contract schema remains large. Test cheaper models by document kind. Measure confidence against actual wrong extractions. Margin step-down and promised credits have arithmetic regressions, but need live extraction cases. Novel waiver wording, units and layouts remain the main uncertainties.
 
 ## Verification after the grader-trap review
 
 `make eval` uses the grader's isolated replay: fresh processes, restricted environment, incremental batches and reports before feedback. Every report's schema, keys and citations are checked. Timeline expectations cover `retro`, `supersedes`, `learned_at`, source documents and forbidden outbound text. Eight old expectations incorrectly used June feedback in earlier reports; positive dates were corrected and pre-decision controls added.

 def column_pdf(head, cols, rows):

     with pymupdf.open() as doc:
         page = doc.new_page(width=595, height=842)
         for n, line in enumerate(head):
             page.insert_text((30, 45 + n * 16), line, fontsize=8)
         xs = [30, 100, 255, 325, 405, 485]
         for n, cells in enumerate([cols, *rows], len(head)):
             y = 45 + n * 16
             for x, text in zip(xs, cells):
                 page.insert_text((x, y), str(text), fontsize=8)
             page.draw_line((25, y + 4), (565, y + 4), color=(0.65, 0.65, 0.65), width=0.5)
         return doc.tobytes()

 """The reading half: Claude turns each document into typed facts. It never decides a verdict, an amount or an action.
 
 One call per email (its facts, and what kind of document each attachment is), then one call per attachment with the
 schema for its kind. The model cites lines by their [page:line] tag instead of copying text, so every quote we later
 put in the report is the page's own text. Answers are cached by content hash: a document is read once.
 """
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 import base64
 import hashlib
 import json
 import os
 import sys
 import time
 from pathlib import Path
 
 MODEL = "claude-opus-5-5"
 PROMPT_VERSION = "v1"

 def cache_dir(state_dir: Path) -> Path:
     """Next to the code when we can write there (one cache for every run on this machine), else in the state dir."""

 _degraded: set = set()               # request features the API refused once: not sent again in this process
 
 
 def _call(content: list, schema: dict, max_tokens: int, effort: str) -> dict:
     """One extraction call -> the schema's JSON. Structured outputs with the server-side refusal fallback; if the API
     refuses either feature (an account without the beta, a schema it won't compile), drop it and keep going, checking
     the JSON against the schema ourselves. Retries a refusal, a truncated answer or invalid JSON."""
     import anthropic
     import jsonschema
     last = None
     for attempt in range(4):
         kw = {"model": MODEL, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "system": SYSTEM,
               "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}], "output_config": {"effort": effort}}
         if "format" not in _degraded:
             kw["output_config"]["format"] = {"type": "json_schema", "schema": schema}
         else:
             kw["messages"] = [{"role": "user", "content": content + [{"type": "text", "text":
                               "Answer with one JSON object matching this JSON Schema, and nothing else:\n"
                               + json.dumps(schema)}]}]
         if "fallbacks" not in _degraded:
             kw.update(betas=["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"], fallbacks="default")
         try:
             with client().beta.messages.stream(**kw) as stream:
                 msg = stream.get_final_message()
         except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
             # a gateway may refuse a feature in its own words: drop the optional ones this request sent, in turn
             sent = [x for x in ("fallbacks", "format") if x in kw or x in kw["output_config"]]
             if not sent:
                 raise                       # nothing optional was sent: a real bad request
             drop = "format" if "format" in sent and any(w in str(e).lower() for w in ("schema", "format")) else sent[0]
             if not any(x in _degraded for x in sent):   # another thread may already have dropped one: then retry
                 _degraded.add(drop)
             last = f"dropped {drop} after: {str(e)[:200]}"
             continue
         if msg.stop_reason == "refusal":
             last = f"refused ({getattr(msg.stop_details, 'category', None)})"
         elif msg.stop_reason == "max_tokens":
             last, max_tokens = "ran out of tokens", min(max_tokens * 2, 128000)
         else:
             text = next((b.text for b in msg.content if b.type == "text"), "")
             text = text.strip().removeprefix("```json").removeprefix("```").removesuffix("```").strip()
             try:
                 out = json.loads(text)
                 jsonschema.validate(out, schema)
                 out["_usage"] = {"in": msg.usage.input_tokens, "out": msg.usage.output_tokens}
                 return out
             except (json.JSONDecodeError, jsonschema.ValidationError) as e:
                 last = f"bad JSON: {str(e)[:200]}"
         time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
     raise RuntimeError(f"extraction failed: {last}")
 
 
 def cached(state_dir: Path, key: str, fn):
     path = cache_dir(state_dir) / f"{hashlib.sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest()[:32]}.json"
     if path.exists() and not os.environ.get("NOVA_NO_CACHE"):     # NOVA_NO_CACHE=1: a live smoke test of the API
         return json.loads(path.read_text())
     out = fn()
     if out:                                  # never cache an empty answer: it would read as a hit next time
         path.write_text(json.dumps(out))
     return out
 
 
 def extract(state_dir: Path, kind: str, sha: str, numbered_text: str, context: str = "") -> dict:
     """Facts of one document of `kind`, as the schema for that kind."""
     def run():
         content = [{"type": "text", "text": f"{INSTRUCTIONS[kind]}\n\n{context}\n\n<document>\n{numbered_text}\n"
                                             f"</document>".replace("\n\n\n", "\n\n")}]
         return _call(content, SCHEMAS[kind], MAX_TOKENS.get(kind, 16000), EFFORT.get(kind, "low"))
     return cached(state_dir, ckey(kind, sha), run)
 
 
 TRANSCRIBE = """This is a scanned page with no text layer. Transcribe every line of text on it, top to bottom, each \
 line left to right with single spaces between the words and columns, exactly as printed (keep thousands separators, \
 decimals, dates and symbols as they appear). Return one string per printed line."""
 
 
 def transcribe(state_dir: Path, sha: str, pngs: list[bytes]) -> list[str]:
     """A scan's pages as text lines (our own text layer: the grader can't check quotes on a scan, only the page)."""
     def run():
         pages = []
         for png in pngs:
             content = [{"type": "image", "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": "image/png",
                                                     "data": base64.standard_b64encode(png).decode()}},
                        {"type": "text", "text": TRANSCRIBE}]
             out = _call(content, O(lines=A(S())), 16000, "low")
             pages.append("\n".join(out["lines"]))
         return {"pages": pages}
     return cached(state_dir, ckey("scan", sha), run)["pages"]

 def sourced(f):
     if isinstance(f, dict):
         f = {k: sourced(v) for k, v in f.items()}
         f.setdefault("src_q", {"page": 1, "quote": "Independently authored regression document facts."})
     elif isinstance(f, list):
         f = [sourced(v) for v in f]
     return f
 
 
 def contract(cid="C", currency="USD"):
     return sourced({"contract_id": cid, "carrier_party": "CAR", "shipper_party": "BUY", "currency": currency,
                     "signed_by_both": True, "effective_date": "2040-01-01", "end_date": "2042-12-31",
                     "rates": [{"lane": lane, "lo": "0", "hi": None, "period_rates": [{"period": "", "rate": rate}]}
                               for lane, rate in (("A-B", "3"), ("A-C", "2"))],
                     "charge_codes": [{"code": code, "name": name, "aliases": []} for code, name in
                                      (("FRT", "Freight"), ("MARGIN", "Handling margin"), ("COST", "Carrier cost"),
                                       ("ACCT", "Account fee"), ("TAX", "Tax"))],
                     "authorised_persons": [{"name": "Dana Disputes", "party": "CAR", "categories": ["billing_disputes"],
                                             "email": "disputes@car.example"},
                                            {"name": "Kai Account", "party": "CAR", "title": "Key Account Manager",
                                             "categories": ["notices"], "email": "kai@car.example"}],
                     "clauses": {"qualifying_spend": {"include_codes": ["FRT", "COST"], "include_annex_d": False,
                                                        "net_of_credit_notes": True},
                                 "late_fee": {"percent_per_month": "1", "grace_days": 3}}})
 
 
 def invoice(no, when="2040-03-10", *, cid="C", currency="USD", awb=None, lane="A-B", rate="4", qty="100", lines=None):
     if lines is None:
         lines = [{"awb": awb or f"AWB-{no}", "lane": lane, "date": when, "description": "Freight", "quantity": qty,
                   "rate": rate, "amount": str(E.rhu(E.D(qty) * E.D(rate)))}]
     return sourced({"invoice_number": no, "invoice_date": when, "contract_id": cid, "currency": currency,
                     "lines": lines, "total": E.money(sum((E.D(x["amount"]) for x in lines), E.ZERO))})
 
 
 def credit(amount, when, *, cid="C", kind="dispute", period=None, lines=None):
     return sourced({"number": f"CN-{when}", "contract_id": cid, "credit_date": when, "currency": "USD",
                     "credit_type": kind, "period": period, "lines": lines or [], "total": str(amount),
                     "total_src_q": {"page": 1, "quote": f"Total credit USD {amount}, issued on {when}."}})
 
 
 def feedback(decision, *, fid="fb-1", key=None, fact=None, filters=None, kind="standing", start="2040-03-01",
              end="2040-06-30", decided="2040-05-01"):
     return {"item_id": fid, "decision": decision, "finding_key": key or {"invoice_id": "OLD", "class": "overcharge"},
             "fact": fact or {}, "scope": {"kind": kind, "applies_to": filters or {}, "valid_from": start,
                                          "valid_to": end}, "_batch": "batch_01", "_decided_at": decided}
 
 
 def store(state, records):
     folder = Path(state) / "docs"
     folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
     for n, rec in enumerate(records):
         kind, facts, received, *sender = rec
         name, addr = sender[0] if sender else ("Billing", "billing@car.example")
         ref = f"batch_01/{n:04d}.eml"
         data = {"meta": {"received": received + "T12:00:00Z", "email": ref, "from_name": name, "from_addr": addr},
                 "docs": [{"ref": ref + f"#{n}.pdf", "kind": kind, "facts": facts}]}
         (folder / f"{n:04d}.json").write_text(json.dumps(data))
 
 
 def build(records, as_of="2040-05-15", fb=(), mode="supervised"):
     with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
         store(tmp, records)
         return E.build(Path(tmp), date.fromisoformat(as_of), mode, list(fb), {})
 
 
 def items(report):
     return {E.key_of(it): it for it in report["findings"] + [it for xs in report["portfolio"].values() for it in xs]}

         from decimal import Decimal
         for printed, amount in (("300.00 CR", "-300"), ("300.00CR", "-300"), ("300.00 DR", "300"), ("45,50-", "-45.50"),
                                 ("\u2212USD 1,200.50", "-1200.50"), ("CAD 1 234,56", "1234.56"),

---

**1. Invoice line net amount (§10.2.2, BT-131; rule PEPPOL-EN16931-R120)**
Rule: Line net amount = (Item net price ÷ Item price base quantity) × Invoiced quantity + line charge amount − line allowance amount. It is the VAT-exclusive amount, inclusive of line-level allowances/charges; each part of the calculation is rounded to two decimals separately.
Verbatim: *"The invoice line net amount (BT-131) is as the name implies the **net** amount without VAT, and inclusive of line level allowance and charges."*
Formula (verbatim): *"Item line net amount=((Item net price (BT-146)÷Item price base quantity (BT-149))×(Invoiced Quantity (BT-129))+Invoice line charge amount (BT-141)-Invoice line allowance amount (BT-136)"*
Rule (verbatim): *"[PEPPOL-EN16931-R120]-Invoice line net amount MUST equal (Invoiced quantity \* (Item net price/item price base quantity) + Sum of invoice line charge amount - sum of invoice line allowance amount"* (closing paren is missing in the source) — and *"the different parts of the calculation must be rounded separately."*

**2. Price base quantity (§10.2.2, BT-149; rules R121/R130)**
Rule: The Item net price is stated per base quantity, so the effective unit price is net price ÷ base quantity before multiplying by the invoiced quantity. Base quantity must be positive and above zero, and its unit of measure must match the invoiced quantity's unit.
Verbatim: *"Invoice line net amount=((Item net price÷Item price base quantity)×(Invoiced Quantity)"*; *"[PEPPOL-EN16931-R121]-Base quantity MUST be a positive number above zero."*; *"[PEPPOL-EN16931-R130]-Unit code of price base quantity MUST be same as invoiced quantity."*

**3. Document-level allowances/charges and "Tax exclusive amount" (§10.1, §10.1.1; rule BR-CO-13)**
Rule: "Tax exclusive amount" is the UBL element `cbc:TaxExclusiveAmount`, i.e. the Invoice total amount without VAT (BT-109): sum of line net amounts (BT-106) minus document-level allowances (BT-107) plus document-level charges (BT-108). Each doc-level allowance/charge amount (when base amount and percentage are present) = Base amount × (Percentage ÷ 100).
Verbatim (BR-CO-13): *"Invoice total amount without VAT (BT-109) = Σ Invoice line net amount (BT-131) - Sum of allowances on document level (BT-107) + Sum of charges on document level (BT-108)."*
Verbatim (UBL): *"TaxExclusiveAmount ... LineExtensionAmount – AllowanceTotalAmount + ChargeTotalAmount"*
Verbatim (§10.3): *"Amount=Base amount×(Percentage÷100)"*

**4. Prepaid amounts and Amount due for payment (§10.1, BT-115; rule BR-CO-16)**
Rule: Amount due for payment (BT-115) = Invoice total amount with VAT (BT-112) − Paid amount (BT-113, the prepaid amount) + Rounding amount (BT-114). In UBL: PayableAmount = TaxInclusiveAmount − PrepaidAmount + PayableRoundingAmount; PrepaidAmount has no calculation formula ("Not applicable") — it is a given input.
Verbatim (BR-CO-16): *"Amount due for payment (BT-115) = Invoice total amount with VAT (BT-112) -Paid amount (BT-113) +Rounding amount (BT-114)."*

**5. Document-level rounding / payable rounding amount (§9, §10.1.2)**
Rule: All document-level amounts are rounded to two decimals; results of calculations over already-rounded amounts (payable amounts, totals incl. VAT) are not re-rounded. `cbc:PayableRoundingAmount` is a header-level element used to round the expected payable amount and is added to PayableAmount.
Verbatim: *"All document level amounts shall be rounded to two decimals for accounting"*; *"Results from calculations involving already rounded amounts are not subject to rounding, like payable amounts and total amounts included VAT."*; *"It is possible to round the expected payable amount."*; *"Example: Amount 999.81 rounded to 1000. PayableRounding Amount = 0.19"*

**6. Credit notes / negative amounts (§5.6, §5.6.1, §5.6.2)**
Rule: The BIS supports negative grand totals. With a credit note (type code 381), crediting is conveyed by the document type while amounts keep their sign; with a negative invoice (type 380), crediting is conveyed by the sign of the amounts. In both cases the unit price is never made negative.
Verbatim (§5.6.1): *"The function of crediting or debiting is controlled merely by the business document type (e.g. 380 or 381)"* [continues: *"while the representation of the amount, including its sign, is not affected."*]
Verbatim (§5.6.2): *"The function of crediting or debiting is controlled merely by the sign (i.e. plus sign or minus sign) of the amount concerned"*
Verbatim (price): *"Price amount must always be positive, and is not changed"* (annotation to the negative-invoice example)
Also: *"this BIS supports negative grand totals in order to open up for a wider spectrum of invoicing processes."*

**7. VAT category codes / breakdown (§8.3, §10.4, §12.1.4; rules BR-48, BR-CO-17)**
Rule: Note — the exact term "VAT category amount" does not appear in the document; the actual terms are VAT category code (BT-118), VAT category rate (BT-119), VAT category taxable amount (BT-116), and VAT category tax amount (BT-117). One VAT breakdown exists per distinct code+rate combination (trailing zeros in the rate don't create a new group); BT-116 = Σ line net amounts (of that category) + doc-level charges − doc-level allowances, and BT-117 = BT-116 × rate/100, rounded to two decimals. Code list (subset of UN/CEFACT 5305): AE (reverse charge), E (exempt), S (standard), Z (zero rated), G (export outside EU), O (not subject to VAT), K (intra-community), L (Canary Islands), M (Ceuta and Melilla).

Verbatim (BR-48): *"Each VAT breakdown (BG-23) shall have a VAT category rate (BT-119), except if the Invoice is not subject to VAT."*
Verbatim (BR-CO-17): *"VAT category tax amount (BT-117) = VAT category taxable amount (BT-116) x (VAT category rate (BT-119) / 100), rounded to two decimals."*
Verbatim (§10.4): *"VAT category taxable amount (BT-116)=∑(Invoice line net amounts (BT-131)) +Document level charge amount (BT-99)-Document level allowance amount (BT-92)"* and *"For VAT Breakdown where the VAT Category is "Not subject to VAT" (O), the VAT category tax amount shall be zero."*

    return [lines], f

def column_pdf(head, cols, rows):
    """Real positioned cells, not one prejoined paragraph. Match the grader's baseline grouping on extraction."""
    with pymupdf.open() as doc:

def credit_against(w: World, inv_ids: list[str], lines: list[dict]) -> Decimal:
    """Credit notes that reverse what was billed twice: credited in full leaves nothing, in part reduces it. A credit
    note with lines counts only its lines on the duplicated waybills; one without counts when it names the invoice."""
    total = ZERO
    awbs = {norm_awb(ln.get("awb")) for ln in lines} - {""}
    for cn in w.credit_notes:
        if cn.get("credit_type") not in ("dispute", "other", None):
            continue
        cls = cn.get("lines") or []
        hit = [x for x in cls if norm_awb(x.get("awb")) in awbs]
        if hit:
            total += sum((abs(D(x.get("amount")) or ZERO) for x in hit), ZERO)
        elif not any(x.get("awb") for x in cls) and {norm_inv(x) for x in cn.get("invoice_numbers") or []} & set(inv_ids):
            total += abs(D(cn.get("total")) or ZERO)
    return total
```

commercial_invoice:
    url: https://www.ups.com/us/en/shipping/international-shipping/commercial-invoice
    issuer: UPS
    title: How to Create a Commercial Invoice
    inspected: Search-index page excerpt
    observations:
      - A commercial invoice describes product values for customs; it is not a bill for carrier freight services.
  peppol_bis:
    url: https://docs.peppol.eu/poacc/billing/3.0/bis/
    issuer: OpenPeppol
    title: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0
    inspected: Full page text, retrieved 2026-10-15
    observations:
      - "Line net amount = (item net price / price base quantity) x invoiced quantity + line charges - line "
        "allowances (rule R120); the parts round separately."
      - "Total without VAT = sum of line net amounts - document allowances + document charges (BR-CO-13)."
      - "Amount due = total with VAT - prepaid amount + rounding amount (BR-CO-16); rounding is a header-level "
        "amount, e.g. 999.81 rounded to 1000 gives 0.19."
      - Price amount is always positive; crediting is conveyed by document type (credit note) or by amount sign, so
        a note can mix negative cancellation lines with positive re-billed lines.
      - One VAT breakdown per distinct category code and rate; tax = taxable amount x rate / 100, rounded to cents.
  fedex_edi_210:
    url: https://www.fedex.com/content/dam/fedex/us-united-states/services/210_motor_carrier_freight_details_invoice_and_820_payment_order-remittance_advice.pdf
    issuer: FedEx
    title: "EDI Invoicing Implementation Guide: 210 Invoice Detail, 820 Payment Order/Remittance Advice"
    inspected: Pages 1-7 of 54 (contents and introduction)
    observations:
      - One invoice transaction set carries many tracking numbers, one per LX loop; multi-shipment invoices are the
        norm and detail tracking data sits inside each loop.
      - The guide has a dedicated late-fee segment syntax and a sample late-fee-only invoice (contents pages 23-25):
        an invoice can contain nothing but late fees.
      - Electronic Invoice Adjustment files with reason codes adjust billed charges as separate documents.
      - Duty and tax invoicing follows its own rules, separate from transportation charges.
  fedex_india_gst:
    url: https://www.fedex.com/en-in/billing/gst.html
    issuer: FedEx India
    title: Goods and Services Tax (GST)
    inspected: Search-index page excerpt
    observations:
      - FedEx India collects GST registration details and GSTIN so invoices carry the correct GST; Indian freight
        invoices show GST (as CGST, SGST and IGST) alongside transport charges.
  dhl_french:
    url: https://www.dhl.com/discover/fr-ma/ship-with-dhl/start-shipping/paying-your-dhl-invoice
    issuer: DHL Express
    title: Paiement de votre facture DHL
    inspected: Full article, plus search excerpt of the French general conditions PDF
    observations:
      - French-language billing uses facture / avoir / TVA / echeance vocabulary; MyBill exports CSV for accounting.
      - The French general conditions provide for a facture rectificative (corrective invoice) when VAT was omitted
        from the original invoice.
  factur_x:
    url: https://www.ferd-net.de/fileadmin/user_upload/FeRD/Downloads/Press_Release_Factur-X_1.07.3_ZUGFeRD_2.3.3.pdf
    issuer: FeRD
    title: New Patch-Release of the Franco-German E-Invoice Format Factur-X/ZUGFeRD
    inspected: Search-index excerpt
    observations:
      - Factur-X/ZUGFeRD is a hybrid e-invoice: a PDF/A-3 file with an embedded XML part; the PDF layer is the
        human-readable representation and the XML the machine-readable one.
  format_scope_note:
    observation: grader/extract.py reads only .pdf, .xlsx and .eml attachments; CSV and XML e-invoice attachments
      are not citable documents, so the harness leaves them unparsed and a hybrid Factur-X invoice is read through
      its PDF layer.

Golden facts and cached mailbox passes do not establish live extraction quality or a hidden score.

input.newString:
## What works

Measured on cached extractions: the practice card is 99.8 out of 100 in supervised and in autonomous mode, with every hard gate clear; all 46 eval cases pass (2 shipped samples and 44 of mine over 23 mailboxes: new customer, wordings and layouts, an injection email, one-off and quoted waivers, a backdated amendment, compounding late fees, the 14-day and 60-day windows, storage and delivery rules, partial credits, INR without an exchange rate, and sixteen feedback cases for resolve, override, close, reject and standing or one-off authority, including controls that check feedback does *not* act before its decision date). The exam sheet comes out at $8,165.33 total savings; I rederived all ten findings by hand from the documents, including the scanned INR invoice (its transcription is arithmetically self-consistent) and the cashback quarter. Every quote in both reports resolves with the grader's validator. Invoice arithmetic checks pass on all 112 cached invoices and fire on a mutated number.

Beyond the cases, two offline suites exercise the rules directly. `make test` runs 27 typed-fact regressions with no API: the close/learn/sibling rate triple, every feedback scope filter and date boundary, a later backdated amendment beating an accepted notice, exactly-$5,000 invoice aggregation across classes, stale late-fee risk removal, the three credit types (including thresholds net of prior credit notes and a retransmitted credit note counted once), sign and currency renderings, and adversarial reports pushed through the real scorer with all five hard gates asserted clear. `make eval` itself no longer checks a single final report: it replays each case through `grader/run_grader.py`'s own stepper (fresh processes, empty working directory, restricted environment, a report before every feedback delivery) and validates the schema, duplicate keys and every citation of every report, plus timeline facts (`supersedes`, `learned_at`, `retro`, forbidden outbound text). That strictness is what caught the eight stale expectations below.

`make eval-web` builds 28 fictional invoice layouts from public carrier documentation (UPS, DHL, IATA, Maersk, LTL guides, Peppol BIS Billing 3.0, the FedEx EDI 210 guide, FedEx India GST, DHL French billing, Factur-X; provenance and what was inspected in `evals/web_sources.yaml`) and replays them in both modes with explicit golden extraction facts. The corpus covers published/incentive/net-billed columns, correction deltas, credit-then-rebill cycles, resent credit notes, piece versus billed weights, CWT and PRO references, container-level charges, monetary per-pound fuel, contract-defined fuel bases, prepaid/collect allocation, document-level allowances with applied prepaid and rounding, a French TVA layout with HT/TTC totals, an Indian GST invoice with CGST/SGST/IGST, a late-fee-only invoice with an authorised due-date extension, and a hybrid Factur-X PDF with embedded XML, plus decoys (customs commercial invoice, pro forma, deficit weight, remittance repetitions) and an injected remittance footer. Each case also asserts the parsed invoice ids, line counts and totals, so a negative case cannot pass by ignoring the document.

## What doesn't

- **No real API call has been made from this code.** Everything behind these numbers was read by Claude Code subagents (Opus, later Sonnet) using the same prompts and schemas, written into the same cache; the SDK path was exercised only against a local stand-in endpoint (above). What a real `claude-opus-5-5` reads from your documents, and how long a large contract takes against the 600-second step limit, are untested. This is the biggest risk for your run.
- The same limit covers the new suites: `make eval-web` and the regressions run on authored golden facts and cached extractions, so they prove the rules, the process boundaries and the reader *prompts*, not what a live model reads from an unseen layout. `make eval-web LIVE=1` exists for exactly that and has not been run (no key here).
- The practice score is a smoke test: the answers are public and I tuned to them. The exam sheet has no key, so I can only say its numbers are internally right, not that nothing is missing.
- Margin step-down, other promised credits, band-by-band and annual rebates are implemented with offline regressions, but no contract in the data has those clauses, so how they are worded and extracted is untested.
- The engine went through two adversarial reviews against GLOSSARY.md (27 confirmed bugs, then 18 problems in those fixes, all fixed and replayed), then a review against the grader's own scoring code; late-fee and conflict edge cases beyond those are still the least-tested code.
- Confidence is hand-set. The local sets have no reported wrong item, so AUROC and Brier could not be tuned.
- My evals were written by me with knowledge of the engine. They test generalisation to new wordings, not to the unknown.

## The eval case that caught a bug

`ev_conflict_above_both` and the shipped `sample_conflict` both came back `cannot_determine` instead of `conflict`. The cause: an amendment that replaces a lane's rates inline also names "Annex A", and my rule read any named rates document we don't hold as missing. The fix makes a reference count as missing only when the instrument gives no rates for that lane itself and the name isn't part of the contract we do hold. It fixed three cases at once and left the practice card unchanged. A second catch was in my own tooling: a cache helper wrote empty results, which then looked like hits, so one contract silently read as `unreadable`.

Later passes caught four more. Moving `make eval` onto the grader's own replay exposed eight feedback cases that expected a person's June 1 decision to change a March or May 31 report — the eval runner had only ever looked at one final report, so the dates were never checked; the positive dates moved after the decision and pre-decision controls were added. A resent-credit fixture showed the same credit note subtracted twice from cashback; credit notes are now deduplicated by contract and printed id. A Peppol-style note mixing a −100 cancellation with a +25 re-bill was subtracted as 125 instead of 75 because the code took the absolute value of every line; mixed-sign notes now count their net. And the French and GST layouts came back empty because their printed charge labels ("Fret principal", "Air freight") matched no code alias — the fixture contracts now define the labels they use, which is the honest fix: a contract, not a hardcoded list, is where labels come from.

 def column_pdf(head, cols, rows):
     """Real positioned cells, not one prejoined paragraph. Match the grader's baseline grouping on extraction."""
     with pymupdf.open() as doc:
         page = doc.new_page(width=595, height=842)
         for n, line in enumerate(head):
             page.insert_text((30, 45 + n * 16), line, fontsize=8)
         xs = [30, 100, 255, 325, 405, 485]
         for n, cells in enumerate([cols, *rows], len(head)):
             y = 45 + n * 16
             for x, text in zip(xs, cells):
                 page.insert_text((x, y), str(text), fontsize=8)
             page.draw_line((25, y + 4), (565, y + 4), color=(0.65, 0.65, 0.65), width=0.5)
         return doc.tobytes()

     def write(self):
         folder = BASE / self.name / "batch_01"
         folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
         golden = {}
         for n, doc in enumerate(self.documents, 1):
             path = folder / f"{n:04d}.eml"

                                  "Please find the referenced document attached. Aurora Freight.", [(name, blob)]))
             email, att = DOCS.read_email(path, "batch_01")

                 {"name": name, "kind": ("invoice" if wrong is True else wrong if isinstance(wrong, str) else kind)}],
                 "requests_payment": "yes"}}

                                                         if d[2] == "credit_note"})},

input.command:
git commit -m "Harden harness against grader traps; add source-backed layout corpus and regressions

- Feedback: unavailable before its decision date; scope filters fail closed; one-off
  approvals cover only their named key/months; later signed amendments beat older
  feedback; a later override can reopen a closed key; changed items carry learned_at.
- Autonomous checks shared across detectors (repricing, waivers, duplicates, credits):
  trusted pickups, consistent arithmetic, Schedule 1 recipient, conflict and threshold
  gates; per-quantity fuel bases and unit handling; mixed-sign credit notes count net;
  resent credit notes deduplicated by contract and printed id; resent partial credits
  no longer double-subtracted.
- eval runner replays through grader/run_grader.py (fresh processes, restricted env,
  report before feedback) and validates schema, duplicate keys, citations and timeline
  facts per report; 46/46 cases pass.
- New make eval-web: 28 source-backed invoice layouts (UPS, DHL, IATA, Maersk, LTL,
  Peppol BIS, FedEx EDI/GST, French TVA, Factur-X) with golden reading, 56/56 checks,
  live-reader mode behind LIVE=1.
- make test: offline typed-fact regressions incl. adversarial reports clearing all
  five scorer gates; extraction failures fail ingest instead of passing silently.
- Docs (SOLUTION/DESIGN/AI_USE) record the work and the four bugs the new evals caught.
- Practice 99.8/100 both modes, all hard gates clear; exam sheet \$8,165.33 unchanged." && git log --oneline -3 && git status --short

Index: SOLUTION.md
===================================================================
--- SOLUTION.md	
+++ SOLUTION.md	
@@ -1,42 +1,50 @@
 # My solution
 
 ## How to run it
 
 ```
 make setup                                   # .venv from harness/requirements.txt
 export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...                 # and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL if you use a gateway
 make grade                                   # practice mailbox, both modes -> report_card.txt / .json
 make sheet                                   # exam mailbox -> out/exam_report.json, answer_sheet.json
 make eval                                    # 46 cases in evals/cases, 44 of them mine
 make test                                    # offline rules regressions, no API needed
 make eval-web                                # 28 source-backed invoice layouts, offline reading
 make validate
 ```
 
 Nothing beyond `harness/requirements.txt` is needed, and nothing but `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`: the harness calls the Anthropic Python SDK (`anthropic==1.8.0`, as shipped) directly; no Claude Code, no `claude` CLI. `ingest` reads each email as its own pipeline (the email, then its attachments in parallel, 12 at a time) and saves it as soon as it is done, so a step cut short keeps what it finished. Each document is one streamed call to `claude-opus-5-5` with structured output; results are cached by content hash in `.cache/llm`, or in the state dir when the code folder is read-only. If the endpoint refuses the server-side fallback beta or the output schema, whatever its error text, the harness drops that feature and checks the JSON against the schema itself. A scan goes to the vision model, with local OCR (`rapidocr`) when that call fails. `make grade` on a cold cache is about 160 calls per mode. `NOVA_NO_CACHE=1` forces live calls (dev only).
 
+## Before you run it
+
+- A key is needed only for `make grade` and `make sheet`. `make eval`, `make test`, `make eval-web` and `make validate` run entirely offline against cached extractions and authored facts, so you can verify the rules without one. Python 3.11 or newer.
+- The harness talks only to `api.anthropic.com`. Expect roughly $40 to $60 per 1,000 documents at list prices ($4 / $20 per million tokens); contracts dominate. The grader gives each step 600 seconds; a cold-cache practice replay is about 160 calls per mode.
+- `.cache/llm/` is a dev-only cache of extractions from the mailbox data. It is gitignored on purpose; never ship it, and `NOVA_NO_CACHE=1` bypasses it.
+- For a first sanity check: a healthy run scores 99.8/100 on practice in both modes with every hard gate clear, and the exam sheet totals $8,165.33 (1 conflict, 1 cannot_determine). `make eval-web LIVE=1` is the only command that reads the new-layout corpus with the real model; everything else is offline by design.
+- If a document can't be read, ingest exits nonzero and says which one — a clean-looking report is never hiding an unreadable document (the report's `diagnostics` block lists what was parsed).
+
 How that path was checked without a key here: a local stand-in for the Messages endpoint, run with only the two environment variables, on a read-only copy of `harness/`. All 41 practice and 41 exam emails went through ingest, report and feedback with nothing unreadable, and so did gateways that reject the fallback beta, reject the schema, or answer with an uninformative 400. It proves the plumbing (request shape, streaming, schema checks, fallbacks, scans, caching), not what a real model reads.
 
 ## What works
 
 Measured on cached extractions: the practice card is 99.8 out of 100 in supervised and in autonomous mode, with every hard gate clear; all 46 eval cases pass (2 shipped samples and 44 of mine over 23 mailboxes: new customer, wordings and layouts, an injection email, one-off and quoted waivers, a backdated amendment, compounding late fees, the 14-day and 60-day windows, storage and delivery rules, partial credits, INR without an exchange rate, and fourteen feedback cases for resolve, override, close, reject and standing or one-off authority, including controls that check feedback does *not* act before its decision date). The exam sheet comes out at $8,165.33 total savings; I rederived all ten findings by hand from the documents, including the scanned INR invoice (its transcription is arithmetically self-consistent) and the cashback quarter. Every quote in both reports resolves with the grader's validator. Invoice arithmetic checks pass on all 112 cached invoices and fire on a mutated number.
 
 Beyond the cases, two offline suites exercise the rules directly. `make test` runs 27 typed-fact regressions with no API: the close/learn/sibling rate triple, every feedback scope filter and date boundary, a later backdated amendment beating an accepted notice, exactly-$5,000 invoice aggregation across classes, stale late-fee risk removal, the three credit types (including thresholds net of prior credit notes and a retransmitted credit note counted once), sign and currency renderings, and adversarial reports pushed through the real scorer with all five hard gates asserted clear. `make eval` itself no longer checks a single final report: it replays each case through `grader/run_grader.py`'s own stepper (fresh processes, empty working directory, restricted environment, a report before every feedback delivery) and validates the schema, duplicate keys and every citation of every report, plus timeline facts (`supersedes`, `learned_at`, `retro`, forbidden outbound text). That strictness is what caught the eight stale expectations below.
 
 `make eval-web` builds 28 fictional invoice layouts from public carrier documentation (UPS, DHL, IATA, Maersk, LTL guides, Peppol BIS Billing 3.0, the FedEx EDI 210 guide, FedEx India GST, DHL French billing, Factur-X; provenance and what was inspected in `evals/web_sources.yaml`) and replays them in both modes with explicit golden extraction facts. The corpus covers published/incentive/net-billed columns, correction deltas, credit-then-rebill cycles, resent credit notes, piece versus billed weights, CWT and PRO references, container-level charges, monetary per-pound fuel, contract-defined fuel bases, prepaid/collect allocation, document-level allowances with applied prepaid and rounding, a French TVA layout with HT/TTC totals, an Indian GST invoice with CGST/SGST/IGST, a late-fee-only invoice with an authorised due-date extension, and a hybrid Factur-X PDF with embedded XML, plus decoys (customs commercial invoice, pro forma, deficit weight, remittance repetitions) and an injected remittance footer. Each case also asserts the parsed invoice ids, line counts and totals, so a negative case cannot pass by ignoring the document.
 
 ## What doesn't
 
 - **No real API call has been made from this code.** Everything behind these numbers was read by Claude Code subagents (Opus, later Sonnet) using the same prompts and schemas, written into the same cache; the SDK path was exercised only against a local stand-in endpoint (above). What a real `claude-opus-5-5` reads from your documents, and how long a large contract takes against the 600-second step limit, are untested. This is the biggest risk for your run.
 - The same limit covers the new suites: `make eval-web` and the regressions run on authored golden facts and cached extractions, so they prove the rules, the process boundaries and the reader *prompts*, not what a live model reads from an unseen layout. `make eval-web LIVE=1` exists for exactly that and has not been run (no key here).
 - The practice score is a smoke test: the answers are public and I tuned to them. The exam sheet has no key, so I can only say its numbers are internally right, not that nothing is missing.
 - Margin step-down, other promised credits, band-by-band and annual rebates are implemented with offline regressions, but no contract in the data has those clauses, so how they are worded and extracted is untested.
 - The engine went through two adversarial reviews against GLOSSARY.md (27 confirmed bugs, then 18 problems in those fixes, all fixed and replayed), then a review against the grader's own scoring code; late-fee and conflict edge cases beyond those are still the least-tested code.
 - Confidence is hand-set. The local sets have no reported wrong item, so AUROC and Brier could not be tuned.
 - My evals were written by me with knowledge of the engine. They test generalisation to new wordings, not to the unknown.
 
 ## The eval case that caught a bug
 
 `ev_conflict_above_both` and the shipped `sample_conflict` both came back `cannot_determine` instead of `conflict`. The cause: an amendment that replaces a lane's rates inline also names "Annex A", and my rule read any named rates document we don't hold as missing. The fix makes a reference count as missing only when the instrument gives no rates for that lane itself and the name isn't part of the contract we do hold. It fixed three cases at once and left the practice card unchanged. A second catch was in my own tooling: a cache helper wrote empty results, which then looked like hits, so one contract silently read as `unreadable`.
 
 Later passes caught four more. Moving `make eval` onto the grader's own replay exposed eight feedback cases that expected a person's June 1 decision to change a March or May 31 report — the eval runner had only ever looked at one final report, so the dates were never checked; the positive dates moved after the decision and pre-decision controls were added. A resent-credit fixture showed the same credit note subtracted twice from cashback; credit notes are now deduplicated by contract and printed id. A Peppol-style note mixing a −100 cancellation with a +25 re-bill was subtracted as 125 instead of 75 because the code took the absolute value of every line; mixed-sign notes now count their net. And the French and GST layouts came back empty because their printed charge labels ("Fret principal", "Air freight") matched no code alias — the fixture contracts now define the labels they use, which is the honest fix: a contract, not a hardcoded list, is where labels come from.

=== page 1 ===
Nova take-home: ﬁnd the money leaking out of freight
invoices
Freight runs on email. A carrier sends an invoice as a PDF. Someone forwards a waiver. A rate changes in an
amendment that nobody opens again. Quillmere Pharma pays hundreds of these invoices a quarter, and
some of them are wrong. Nobody has time to check each one against the contract and the email thread that
changed it, so the money just goes.
We want to see how you'd build something that catches it.
The job
Build an AI harness for Quillmere's accounts payable team: a set of agents that
•  read the mailbox (emails with PDF invoices, Excel statements, contracts and amendments attached);
•  remember what the contracts and emails say, on disk, from one batch of mail to the next;
•  ﬁnd the six kinds of problem below, with the amount and the lines that prove it;
•  raise a conﬂict when two sources that both count disagree, and leave that call to a person;
•  ask when a document they need is missing, and say who holds it;
•  learn from a person's answers to what they escalated;
•  act on their own only when it's safe.
In the practice mailbox Tarrowby Express is the carrier. The exam mailbox and our hidden set bring other
customers and carriers. Every company, person, number and date in the data is made up.
The six classes
1. Overcharge. A line billed above what the contract allowed on the pickup date.
2. Duplicate. The same shipment or charge billed twice, sometimes months apart and worded diﬀerently.
3. Waived but billed. A person with authority waived a charge by email, and it's on the invoice anyway.
4. Late fees. A late fee that isn't owed, or an unpaid invoice that will start costing a fee within 14 days.
5. Cashback and credits. A rebate or credit the contract promises that the carrier never paid.
6. Expiry. A contract that ends, or whose notice deadline falls, in the next 60 days.
Two more behaviours cut across all six. A conﬂict is two trusted sources that disagree. cannot_determine
means the answer depends on a document you don't have. GLOSSARY.md deﬁnes every term, formula and
window. Read it before you write code. It will save you hours.
Three levels
Level 1. Learn from the examples, then pass the practice grader. data/examples/ holds one small
worked example per class, plus a conﬂict and a charge billed again four months later. Each has its
documents, an EXPLANATION.md (the deciding clause, the email line, the arithmetic step by step, and why the
look-alike next to it is ﬁne) and the expected output. data/scenarios/ is the practice mailbox: two batches,
about 160 documents, 30 scenarios, one feedback ﬁle after the ﬁrst batch (data/scenarios/feedback/), and
the answers in data/scenarios/answers/. An answer ﬁle gives the verdict, the amount, the action in each
mode and the evidence after each batch. It doesn't show the arithmetic: the examples do that. Some invoices
are clean and some are built to look wrong, so ﬂagging everything fails. make grade replays the mailbox
through your harness with our grader, feeds in the feedback ﬁle after batch_01, and prints a report card out of
100.
Level 2. Your numbers, from a mailbox with no answers. The practice answers are public, so a practice
score can't tell us much. data/exam/ is a second, smaller mailbox that ships with no answers: about 20
scenarios for a customer and a carrier you haven't met, with their own contracts, people, email habits and
Nova take-home  ·  v0.1.0  ·  cohort dryrun  ·  1 / 12

=== page 2 ===
invoice layout. The problems in it are the same kinds the practice set teaches, so a harness that reads
documents by meaning can solve it, and one tuned to the practice ﬁles can't. make sheet runs your harness
on it and writes answer_sheet.json: for each class the count, the dollars and the invoice ids, then the four
totals, the conﬂicts with both sources, and the cannot_determine items with the missing document and who
holds it. That sheet is Part 1 of your submission. We check it against our key, and it's pass or fail: right
numbers mean we go on to run your code, wrong ones end the review there. It earns no points beyond that.
One exam invoice is a scanned image with no text layer, and it carries one of the exam's ﬁndings: your
harness needs OCR or a vision model to get the sheet right (see "Reading the documents").
Level 3. We run your code on data you haven't seen. Same grader, same commit, many more batches:
three more months of the practice world, then a new world with a new customer and a new carrier. Expect
another invoice layout, a backdated amendment, conﬂicts, a waiver that was only meant once, emails that try
to give your agents orders, and feedback of kinds the practice set doesn't show. We run it in both modes.
A green practice card is where you start
It's easy to get a high practice score and still fail our set. An AI coding tool given only an earlier version of this
repo built a rules-only harness that scored close to full marks on practice in under ﬁfteen minutes, then scored
about 11 out of 100 on our batches. What it had learned was the shape of these particular ﬁles.
Our set is built to catch that. It has a new customer and carrier, with people and contracts you haven't seen,
invoice layouts you haven't seen, documents that come in other wordings and other orders, feedback that has
to be applied to exactly the keys it names, and cases where autonomous mode must hold back. Rules tuned
to the practice ﬁles, like a regex per layout or a list of the names and lanes in this mailbox, will break there.
Treat the practice card as a smoke test. Your own eval set, with layouts, wordings and feedback you write
yourself, is how you ﬁnd out whether your harness generalises.
Getting started
make setup      # .venv with harness/requirements.txt (Python 3.11 or newer; uses uv if you have it)
                # now write harness/harness.py
make grade      # replay the practice mailbox, print the report card (report_card.txt and .json)
make sheet      # run the exam mailbox, write answer_sheet.json
make eval       # run your own cases in evals/
make validate   # check your submission before you send it
The stub harness scores 0 and says which command still raises NotImplementedError. The grader calls
three commands, each in a fresh process (--mode is supervised or autonomous):
python harness/harness.py ingest <batch_dir> --state-dir <dir>
python harness/harness.py report --as-of YYYY-MM-DD --mode supervised --state-dir <dir> > report.json
python harness/harness.py feedback <feedback.json> --state-dir <dir>
Keep everything you learn under --state-dir. The output format is grader/schema/report.schema.json,
and every expected_finding.json in the examples is a valid report you can copy the shape from. Add your

•  read the mailbox (emails with PDF invoices, Excel statements, contracts and amendments attached);
•  remember what the contracts and emails say, on disk, from one batch of mail to the next;
•  ﬁnd the six kinds of problem below, with the amount and the lines that prove it;
•  raise a conﬂict when two sources that both count disagree, and leave that call to a person;
•  ask when a document they need is missing, and say who holds it;
•  learn from a person's answers to what they escalated;
•  act on their own only when it's safe.

customers and carriers. Every company, person, number and date in the data is made up.

1. Overcharge. A line billed above what the contract allowed on the pickup date.

What to send us
Send it within 48 hours of getting the brief. Everything goes in your copy of this repo.
The list
1. Your repo, as a private GitHub repo or a zip. Tell us the commit hash: we grade that commit and nothing
after it.

answer sheet is pass or fail: its numbers have to match our key before we run your code on our set.

eval with your harness's score on them. Tell us in SOLUTION.md which case caught a real bug.
5. DESIGN.md, short enough to print on one side of A4 (about 800 words). It covers your fact model, how you
detect conﬂicts, how you compute conﬁdence, what goes to a person and what autonomous mode is
allowed to do, how feedback changes later behaviour, what happens when new documents arrive, and
your cost per 1,000 documents. The template has a heading for each.

Reply to the email that sent you the brief. Either invite the GitHub account named in that email to your private
repo (read access is enough), or attach a zip of the repo with its .git folder. Put the commit hash in the email.
Don't make the repo public. Don't include your API key anywhere in it.

We want the real log, trimmed only for secrets. Paste it into AI_USE.md, or put the exported ﬁles in ai_log/
and link them from there. A chat export, your tool's session ﬁles or a plain copy and paste all work. If you
wrote some parts without AI, say which. We read the log to see how you split the work between you and the
tools. A tidy log earns nothing extra, and a missing one costs you.

•  AI_USE.md names your tools and has a prompt log, or links to one in ai_log/;
•  nothing in the repo looks like an Anthropic API key.

promised_credit with period: CYn (n counts contract years from the eﬀective date).
•  Once the credit is due, the action is draft:claim_credit. Before its due date, use
internal:track_credit: an earned credit that isn't due yet is still a ﬁnding.
•  Credits already issued. Subtract every credit note for that contract, period and credit type that you hold,
whenever it was issued. A credit the carrier issued before its due date, covering what's owed, leaves
nothing owed: no ﬁnding.
•  Duplicates and spend. Qualifying spend follows the contract's deﬁnition: invoices dated in the period, net
of credit notes dated in the period. A line billed twice counts twice until a credit note reverses it, even while
you're disputing it as a duplicate.
Expiry
Report a contract when its operative date is 0 to 60 days after as_of: 0 <= deadline - as_of <= 60. The
operative date is the end date, or the non-renewal notice deadline when the contract renews itself. An
extension that arrives moves the date, and can take the alert away. The action is internal:alert. Expiry
carries no money.
Totals
•  total_overpayment = overcharge + duplicate + waived_but_billed + late_fee_not_owed
•  cashback_owed = the sum of cashback ﬁndings
•  late_fees_avoided = the sum of late_fee_risk amounts (one month's fee each)
•  total_savings = total_overpayment + cashback_owed + late_fees_avoided
Only finding counts. Conﬂicts and cannot_determine items are listed on their own and add nothing. Findings
sent to human_review still count. In the practice answer ﬁles, in_totals says whether an item adds to the
totals and bucket says which total it adds to (none for expiry and for anything that isn't a ﬁnding).

•  override_amount: use fact.value.amount_usd as the amount of that key (with learned_at).
How to use it without going too far:
1. A standing fact applies to a later key only if every ﬁlter in applies_to matches, inside its dates. The
same person in another category doesn't match. The same lane on another contract doesn't match.
2. A one_off decision changes that one key and nothing else. Approving a waiver for March doesn't waive
April. Applying it to April is one of the ﬁve mistakes that cap your score.
3. A feedback fact counts as level 2 from decided_at: every report after the feedback ﬁle uses it. What it
covers is set by scope: documents and shipments dated inside valid_from to valid_to, even when they
arrived before decided_at. A later signed document on the same subject beats it.
4. close stops that key only. A new invoice with the same wrong rate is a new ﬁnding.
5. Every item that changed because of feedback carries learned_at.

What to send us
Send it within 48 hours of getting the brief. Everything goes in your copy of this repo.
The list
1. Your repo, as a private GitHub repo or a zip. Tell us the commit hash: we grade that commit and nothing
after it.
2. SOLUTION.md, your own write-up: how to run it, what works, what doesn't, and anything we should know
before we run it. The template has a heading for each. Leave README.md, GLOSSARY.md and
BRIEF.pdf as they are: they're the brief, and you keep them.
3. answer_sheet.json from make sheet (the exam mailbox), plus report_card.txt and
report_card.json from make grade (the practice mailbox). Both come from your ﬁnal commit. The
answer sheet is pass or fail: its numbers have to match our key before we run your code on our set.
4. evals/: at least 10 cases of your own beyond our two samples, and evals/results.json from make
eval with your harness's score on them. Tell us in SOLUTION.md which case caught a real bug.
5. DESIGN.md, short enough to print on one side of A4 (about 800 words). It covers your fact model, how you
detect conﬂicts, how you compute conﬁdence, what goes to a person and what autonomous mode is
allowed to do, how feedback changes later behaviour, what happens when new documents arrive, and
your cost per 1,000 documents. The template has a heading for each.
6. AI_USE.md: the AI tools you used, what you used them for, and the prompt log.
How to send it
Reply to the email that sent you the brief. Either invite the GitHub account named in that email to your private
repo (read access is enough), or attach a zip of the repo with its .git folder. Put the commit hash in the email.
Don't make the repo public. Don't include your API key anywhere in it.
The prompt log
We want the real log, trimmed only for secrets. Paste it into AI_USE.md, or put the exported ﬁles in ai_log/
and link them from there. A chat export, your tool's session ﬁles or a plain copy and paste all work. If you
wrote some parts without AI, say which. We read the log to see how you split the work between you and the
tools. A tidy log earns nothing extra, and a missing one costs you.
What make validate checks
Run it before you send. It prints one line per check, and exits 0 only when all of them pass:
•  the harness answers ingest, report and feedback with the arguments the grader passes;
•  every section of SOLUTION.md is ﬁlled in;
•  report_card.json exists and came from make grade;
•  answer_sheet.json exists, came from make sheet, and is dated on the exam mailbox's last report date;
•  out/exam_report.json (written by make sheet) matches the schema, and every quote in it is on the cited
page;
•  evals/cases/ has at least 10 cases besides the samples, and evals/results.json exists;
•  every section of DESIGN.md is ﬁlled in, and it's under about 1,000 words;
•  AI_USE.md names your tools and has a prompt log, or links to one in ai_log/;
•  nothing in the repo looks like an Anthropic API key.
A green make validate means we can grade your submission. How well it scores is up to the grader and to
us.

Interesting: the checker's `SOLUTION_SECTIONS = ["How to run it", "What works", "What doesn't", "The eval case that caught a bug"]` — the four required headings. So the template's fourth "anything we should know before we run it" content was expected to live inside one of those headings (likely in "How to run it" or "What doesn't").

Now the honest answer to the user's question:

1. **How to run it** — YES, present and accurate: make setup, API key env vars, make grade/sheet/eval/test/eval-web/validate, the grader's three commands, cold-cache call count, fallback behavior, NOVA_NO_CACHE.

2. **Anything they would need to know before running** — mostly scattered:
   - The biggest risk is stated in "What doesn't" (no live API call; 600s step limit untested).
   - But things the reviewer genuinely needs to know BEFORE running that are NOT stated in SOLUTION.md:
     - **An API key is required** for make grade/sheet (env var; the harness calls Anthropic SDK). It IS mentioned in the run block ("export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=..."). ✓
     - **Cache behavior**: extractions cached in .cache/llm (dev-only, gitignored); reruns free; `NOVA_NO_CACHE=1` forces live. ✓ stated.
     - **Time**: batch runs take time; 600s per step in grader; untested against live API latency. Partially stated.
     - **Python version**: 3.11+. Stated in Makefile/README but not SOLUTION. Minor.
     - **The web corpus is offline** — golden facts; live path exists (LIVE=1). Stated. ✓
     - **Cost estimate**: ~$40-60/1000 docs — in DESIGN.md, not SOLUTION.
     - **What grading uses**: the reviewer runs grader/run_grader.py with their own key — commit hash matters. Not in SOLUTION (it's in SUBMISSION, which they know).
     - **The harness never needs anything but the SDK** — stated. ✓
     - **make eval/eval-web don't need a key** — not explicitly stated! That's genuinely useful "before you run" info: they can run the offline suites without any key.

So the honest answer: "How to run it" is there, but a consolidated "before you run it" summary is not its own section (the checker doesn't require one — it requires the four headings I have), and a few things a reviewer would want to know before running are scattered or missing:
- offline suites need no key
- .cache is gitignored and contains mailbox read-outs (already in .gitignore comment)
- the 600s/step limit and live latency are untested
- cost estimate per 1,000 docs

I should answer the question directly and honestly first ("mostly yes, but..."), then add a proper consolidated section. Where to put it? Since the checker requires exactly the four headings (extra headings are fine — sections() parses all headings; only the four required need 15+ words), I can add a fifth heading "Before you run it" under "My solution". That satisfies the spirit of the PDF ("anything we should know before we run it. The template has a heading for each" — hmm, "The template has a heading for each" suggests the template had headings for each of the four things; the checker's list is the template's headings. The fourth item "anything we should know before we run it" maps to... the checker has "The eval case that caught a bug" as the 4th. So the template merged "before we run it" into... Actually the README/SUBMISSION says the template has a heading for each of: how to run it, what works, what doesn't, and anything we should know before we run it. But the checker requires: How to run it, What works, What doesn't, The eval case that caught a bug. So the original template evidently had "Before you run it" merged somewhere or the checker's list is what the template had. Nothing beyond `harness/requirements.txt` is needed, and nothing but `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`: the harness calls the Anthropic Python SDK (`anthropic==1.8.0`, as shipped) directly; no Claude Code, no `claude` CLI. `ingest` reads each email as its own pipeline (the email, then its attachments in parallel, 12 at a time) and saves it as soon as it is done, so a step cut short keeps what it finished. Each document is one streamed call to `claude-opus-5-5` with structured output; results are cached by content hash in `.cache/llm`, or in the state dir when the code folder is read-only. If the endpoint refuses the server-side fallback beta or the output schema, whatever its error text, the harness drops that feature and checks the JSON against the schema itself. A scan goes to the vision model, with local OCR (`rapidocr`) when that call fails. `make grade` on a cold cache is about 160 calls per mode. `NOVA_NO_CACHE=1` forces live calls (dev only).

## Before you run it

- A key is needed only for `make grade` and `make sheet`. `make eval`, `make test`, `make eval-web` and `make validate` run entirely offline against cached extractions and authored facts, so you can verify the rules without one. Python 3.11 or newer.
- The harness talks only to `api.anthropic.com`. Expect roughly $40 to $60 per 1,000 documents at list prices ($4 / $20 per million tokens); contracts dominate. The grader gives each step 600 seconds; a cold-cache practice replay is about 160 calls per mode.
- `.cache/llm/` is a dev-only cache of extractions from the mailbox data. It is gitignored on purpose; never ship it, and `NOVA_NO_CACHE=1` bypasses it.
- For a first sanity check: a healthy run scores 99.8/100 on practice in both modes with every hard gate clear, and the exam sheet totals $8,165.33 (1 conflict, 1 cannot_determine). `make eval-web LIVE=1` is the only command that reads the new-layout corpus with the real model; everything else is offline by design.
- If a document can't be read, ingest exits nonzero and says which one — a clean-looking report is never hiding an unreadable document (the report's `diagnostics` block lists what was parsed).

 Measured on cached extractions: the practice card is 99.8 out of 100 in supervised and in autonomous mode, with every hard gate clear; all 46 eval cases pass (2 shipped samples and 44 of mine over 23 mailboxes: new customer, wordings and layouts, an injection email, one-off and quoted waivers, a backdated amendment, compounding late fees, the 14-day and 60-day windows, storage and delivery rules, partial credits, INR without an exchange rate, and fourteen feedback cases for resolve, override, close, reject and standing or one-off authority, including controls that check feedback does *not* act before its decision date).  ## What doesn't
 
 - **No real API call has been made from this code.** Everything behind these numbers was read by Claude Code subagents (Opus, later Sonnet) using the same prompts and schemas, written into the same cache; the SDK path was exercised only against a local stand-in endpoint (above).  - The practice score is a smoke test: the answers are public and I tuned to them. The exam sheet has no key, so I can only say its numbers are internally right, not that nothing is missing.

 ## The eval case that caught a bug
 
 `ev_conflict_above_both` and the shipped `sample_conflict` both came back `cannot_determine` instead of `conflict`. The cause: an amendment that replaces a lane's rates inline also names "Annex A", and my rule read any named rates document we don't hold as missing. The fix makes a reference count as missing only when the instrument gives no rates for that lane itself and the name isn't part of the contract we do hold.
