 def _call(content: list, schema: dict, max_tokens: int, effort: str) -> dict:
     """One extraction call -> the schema's JSON. Structured outputs with the server-side refusal fallback; if the API
     refuses either feature (an account without the beta, a schema it won't compile), drop it and keep going, checking
     the JSON against the schema ourselves. Retries a refusal, a truncated answer or invalid JSON."""
     import anthropic
     import jsonschema
     last = None
     for attempt in range(4):
         kw = {"model": MODEL, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "system": SYSTEM,
               "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}], "output_config": {"effort": effort}}
         if "format" not in _degraded:
             kw["output_config"]["format"] = {"type": "json_schema", "schema": schema}
         else:
             kw["messages"] = [{"role": "user", "content": content + [{"type": "text", "text":
                               "Answer with one JSON object matching this JSON Schema, and nothing else:\n"
                               + json.dumps(schema)}]}]
         if "fallbacks" not in _degraded:
             kw.update(betas=["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"], fallbacks="default")
         try:
             with client().beta.messages.stream(**kw) as stream:
                 msg = stream.get_final_message()
         except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
             # a gateway may refuse a feature in its own words: drop the optional ones this request sent, in turn
             sent = [x for x in ("fallbacks", "format") if x in kw or x in kw["output_config"]]
             if not sent:
                 raise                       # nothing optional was sent: a real bad request
             drop = "format" if "format" in sent and any(w in str(e).lower() for w in ("schema", "format")) else sent[0]
             if not any(x in _degraded for x in sent):   # another thread may already have dropped one: then retry
                 _degraded.add(drop)
             last = f"dropped {drop} after: {str(e)[:200]}"
             continue
         if msg.stop_reason == "refusal":
             last = f"refused ({getattr(msg.stop_details, 'category', None)})"
         elif msg.stop_reason == "max_tokens":
             last, max_tokens = "ran out of tokens", min(max_tokens * 2, 128000)
         else:
             text = next((b.text for b in msg.content if b.type == "text"), "")
             text = text.strip().removeprefix("```json").removeprefix("```").removesuffix("```").strip()
             try:
                 out = json.loads(text)
                 jsonschema.validate(out, schema)
                 out["_usage"] = {"in": msg.usage.input_tokens, "out": msg.usage.output_tokens}
                 return out
             except (json.JSONDecodeError, jsonschema.ValidationError) as e:
                 last = f"bad JSON: {str(e)[:200]}"
         time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
     raise RuntimeError(f"extraction failed: {last}")
 
 
 def cached(state_dir: Path, key: str, fn):
     path = cache_dir(state_dir) / f"{hashlib.sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest()[:32]}.json"
     if path.exists() and not os.environ.get("NOVA_NO_CACHE"):     # NOVA_NO_CACHE=1: a live smoke test of the API
         return json.loads(path.read_text())
     out = fn()
     if out:                                  # never cache an empty answer: it would read as a hit next time
         path.write_text(json.dumps(out))
     return out
 
 
 def extract(state_dir: Path, kind: str, sha: str, numbered_text: str, context: str = "") -> dict:
     """Facts of one document of `kind`, as the schema for that kind."""
     def run():
         content = [{"type": "text", "text": f"{INSTRUCTIONS[kind]}\n\n{context}\n\n<document>\n{numbered_text}\n"
                                             f"</document>".replace("\n\n\n", "\n\n")}]
         return _call(content, SCHEMAS[kind], MAX_TOKENS.get(kind, 16000), EFFORT.get(kind, "low"))
     return cached(state_dir, ckey(kind, sha), run)

     """A scan's pages as text lines (our own text layer: the grader can't check quotes on a scan, only the page)."""
     def run():
         pages = []
         for png in pngs:
             content = [{"type": "image", "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": "image/png",
                                                     "data": base64.standard_b64encode(png).decode()}},
                        {"type": "text", "text": TRANSCRIBE}]

         return {"pages": pages}
     return cached(state_dir, ckey("scan", sha), run)["pages"]

display.text:
# Nova take-home. `make help` lists the targets.
# Every target runs in .venv (made by `make setup`). HARNESS points at your harness; MODE is supervised, autonomous
# or both (the default for make grade).
PY      ?= .venv/bin/python
HARNESS ?= harness/harness.py
MODE    ?= both

.PHONY: help setup venv run grade sheet eval eval-web test validate clean
help:
	@echo "make setup      create .venv and install harness/requirements.txt"
	@echo "make grade      replay the practice mailbox through your harness; writes report_card.txt and .json"
	@echo "make sheet      run the exam mailbox; writes out/exam_report.json and answer_sheet.json"
	@echo "make eval       run your cases in evals/cases (K=<text> runs only matching files)"
	@echo "make test       run offline arithmetic, feedback, action and fresh-process regressions"
	@echo "make eval-web   build/replay source-backed layouts with golden reading (LIVE=1 uses the API)"
	@echo "make validate   check the repo is ready to send (SUBMISSION.md)"
	@echo "make run        run the practice mailbox once; writes out/practice_report.json"

setup:
	@if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
		uv venv -q --allow-existing --python ">=3.11" .venv && uv pip install -q --python .venv/bin/python -r harness/requirements.txt; \
	else \
		python3 -c 'import sys; sys.exit(sys.version_info < (3, 11))' || { echo "need Python 3.11 or newer"; exit 2; }; \
		python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -q -r harness/requirements.txt; \
	fi
	@$(PY) -c "import pymupdf, openpyxl, jsonschema, yaml" && echo "setup done. Next: write harness/harness.py, then make grade"

venv:
	@test -x "$(PY)" || command -v "$(PY)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "no $(PY) yet: run make setup first"; exit 2; }

run: venv
	$(PY) tools/run_mailbox.py --data data/scenarios --harness $(HARNESS) --out out/practice_report.json

grade: venv
	@$(PY) grader/run_grader.py --harness "python $(HARNESS)" --data data/scenarios --key data/scenarios/answers \
		--mode $(MODE) --out report_card.json > report_card.txt; rc=$$?; cat report_card.txt; exit $$rc

sheet: venv
	$(PY) tools/run_mailbox.py --data data/exam --harness $(HARNESS) --out out/exam_report.json --sheet answer_sheet.json

eval: venv
	$(PY) evals/run_evals.py --harness $(HARNESS) $(if $(K),-k $(K),)

test: venv
	$(PY) harness/test_engine.py
	$(PY) harness/test_parse.py
	$(PY) -m unittest discover -s harness -p 'test_regressions.py' -v

eval-web: venv
	$(PY) evals/build_web_cases.py
	$(PY) evals/run_web_evals.py $(if $(filter 1,$(LIVE)),--live,)

validate: venv
	@$(PY) tools/check_submission.py --harness $(HARNESS)

clean:
	rm -rf out/state_* .state

state.output:
### List recent workflow runs with gh run list

Source: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_run_list

Lists recent GitHub Actions workflow runs. Pass `-a` along with `-w` to include disabled workflows.

```shell
gh run list [flags]

```

--------------------------------

### gh run view [<run-id>] [flags]

Source: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_run_view

View a summary of a workflow run, inspect specific jobs, or display execution logs directly in the terminal or browser.

```APIDOC
## gh run view

### Usage
`gh run view [<run-id>] [flags]`

### Description
View a summary of a workflow run. Due to platform limitations, `gh` may not always be able to associate jobs with their corresponding logs when using the primary method of fetching logs in zip format. In such cases, `gh` will attempt to fetch logs for each job individually via the API. If more than 25 job logs are missing, the operation will fail with an error. Some log lines not associated with a specific step will appear as `UNKNOWN STEP`.

### Arguments
- `<run-id>` (optional) - The ID of the workflow run to view.

### Options
- `-a, --attempt <uint>` - The attempt number of the workflow run (default: 0)
- `--exit-status` - Exit with non-zero status if run failed
- `-j, --job <string>` - View a specific job ID from a run
- `-q, --jq <expression>` - Filter JSON output using a jq expression
- `--json <fields>` - Output JSON with the specified fields
- `--log` - View full log for either a run or specific job
- `--log-failed` - View the log for any failed steps in a run or specific job
- `-t, --template <string>` - Format JSON output using a Go template
- `-v, --verbose` - Show job steps
- `-w, --web` - Open run in the browser
- `-R, --repo <[HOST/]OWNER/REPO>` - Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format

### JSON Fields
`attempt`, `conclusion`, `createdAt`, `databaseId`, `displayTitle`, `event`, `headBranch`, `headSha`, `jobs`, `name`, `number`, `startedAt`, `status`, `updatedAt`, `url`, `workflowDatabaseId`, `workflowName`

### Examples
```bash
# Interactively select a run to view, optionally selecting a single job
$ gh run view

# View a specific run
$ gh run view 12345

# View a specific run with specific attempt number
$ gh run view 12345 --attempt 3

# View a specific job within a run
$ gh run view --job 456789

# View the full log for a specific job
$ gh run view --log --job 456789

# Exit non-zero if a run failed
$ gh run view 0451 --exit-status && echo "run pending or passed"
```
```

### gh run

Source: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_run

List, view, and watch recent workflow runs from GitHub Actions.

+"""Run gh with the existing Git credential; never print or persist the credential."""
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+env = dict(os.environ, GH_PROMPT_DISABLED="1", GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT="0")
+if not env.get("GH_TOKEN") and not env.get("GITHUB_TOKEN"):
+    result = subprocess.run(

+    if result.returncode or not fields.get("password"):

+    env["GH_TOKEN"] = fields["password"]

state.output:
### Pass sampling parameters using extra_body for older models

Source: https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/MIGRATION.md

Pass sampling parameters such as temperature using extra_body when targeting older models that still honor them. These parameters were removed from standard method signatures.

```python
# Before
client.messages.create(..., model="claude-sonnet-4-6", temperature=0.2)

# After
client.messages.create(..., model="claude-sonnet-4-6", extra_body={"temperature": 0.2})
```

--------------------------------

### Migrate output_format dict to output_config in beta.messages.create()

Source: https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/MIGRATION.md

Replace the removed output_format parameter with output_config in messages methods, or use helper methods like beta.messages.parse() passing the model class directly.

```python
# Before
client.beta.messages.create(
    ...,
    temperature=0.2,
    output_format={"type": "json_schema", "schema": Order.model_json_schema()},
)

# After
client.beta.messages.create(
    ...,
    output_config={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "schema": Order.model_json_schema()}},
)
# or let the helper build the schema and parse the result:
client.beta.messages.parse(..., output_format=Order)
```

--------------------------------

### Stream message responses with messages.stream

Source: https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/src/anthropic/lib/google_cloud/README.md

Stream text deltas synchronously using the `client.messages.stream` context manager. Tokens are iterated from `stream.text_stream` as they arrive.

```python
with client.messages.stream(
    model="claude-haiku-4-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
) as stream:
    for text in stream.text_stream:
        print(text, end="", flush=True)
```

--------------------------------

### beta.messages.create with fallbacks and beta header

Source: https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/examples/fallbacks.py

Shows calling beta.messages.create on the beta namespace, passing the fallbacks list of model names and the betas header for server-side fallback support.

```python
client = Anthropic()
message = client.beta.messages.create(
    max_tokens=1024,
    model="claude-fable-5",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Some prompt that triggers a refusal"}],
    fallbacks=[{"model": "claude-opus-4-8"}],
    betas=["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"],
)
```

### Tests > How to test

Source: https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/CLAUDE.md

- **Go through the public API.** Mock HTTP with `respx` or an `httpx2.MockTransport`, and assert on the wire request and headers. Don't use `MagicMock` or call private methods, because those tests keep passing when the wire behaviour breaks.
- **Use the shared fixtures.** Use the `client` and `async_client` fixtures from `tests/conftest.py`. They point at `TEST_API_BASE_URL` and accept a strict-validation parameter. Build your own client only when the test needs specific client arguments.
- **Use pytest tools:** `monkeypatch.setenv`, `pytest.mark.parametrize`, and `pytest.mark.skipif`.
- **Streaming cases go in the fixture-based tests.** Add them to `tests/lib/streaming/`, which replays recorded responses from `fixtures/`. Don't start a new test file for them.

state.output:
### Trigger deployment workflow on push, pull_request, and workflow_dispatch

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/control-deployments

Triggers a deployment workflow on pushes or pull requests targeting the main branch, or when manually invoked using workflow_dispatch.

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:
```

--------------------------------

### Configure conditional job execution in GitHub Actions with if

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/migrate-to-github-actions/manual-migrations/migrate-from-gitlab-cicd

Uses the `if` conditional key with `contains` to prevent a job from executing unless a condition is met.

```yaml
jobs:
  deploy_prod:
    if: contains( github.ref, 'master')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Deploy to production server"
```

--------------------------------

### Passing secrets as action inputs and environment variables

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets?tool=cli

Use the `secrets` context to pass repository secrets as action inputs under `with:` or environment variables under `env:`. If a secret is unset, expressions referencing it evaluate to an empty string.

```yaml
steps:
  - name: Hello world action
    with: # Set the secret as an input
      super_secret: ${{ secrets.SuperSecret }}
    env: # Or as an environment variable
      super_secret: ${{ secrets.SuperSecret }}

```

--------------------------------

### Create a starter GitHub Actions workflow in github-actions-demo.yml

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/get-started/quickstart

Save this workflow in `.github/workflows/github-actions-demo.yml` to run automatically when a push event occurs. It runs on `ubuntu-latest`, checks out repository code using `actions/checkout@v6`, and prints context variables and runner details.

```yaml
name: GitHub Actions Demo
run-name: ${{ github.actor }} is testing out GitHub Actions 🚀
on: [push]
jobs:
  Explore-GitHub-Actions:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "🎉 The job was automatically triggered by a ${{ github.event_name }} event."
      - run: echo "🐧 This job is now running on a ${{ runner.os }} server hosted by GitHub!"
      - run: echo "🔎 The name of your branch is ${{ github.ref }} and your repository is ${{ github.repository }}."
      - name: Check out repository code
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - run: echo "💡 The ${{ github.repository }} repository has been cloned to the runner."
      - run: echo "🖥️ The workflow is now ready to test your code on the runner."
      - name: List files in the repository
        run: |
          ls ${{ github.workspace }}
      - run: echo "🍏 This job's status is ${{ job.status }}."

```

--------------------------------

### Running a step with an if conditional expression

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/migrate-to-github-actions/manual-migrations/migrate-from-travis-ci

Applies an `if` expression to conditionally execute a step only when environment variables match specified values. GitHub Actions skips the step if the condition evaluates to false.

```yaml
jobs:
  conditional:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "This step runs with str equals 'ABC' and num equals 123"
        if: env.str == 'ABC' && env.num == 123
```

+

**Fixed, pushed, and verified: [CI is green](https://github.com/HelloSniperMonkey/hope-it-works/actions/runs/38642817473).**

The failure was an empty `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`: CI attempted live grading without credentials or the local extraction cache.

Push CI now runs:
- **28** offline regressions
- **56** golden-reader layout checks
- Submission artifact validation

Live grading is a separate manual option. To use it, add the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` repository secret, then select **Actions → checks → Run workflow → live_grade**.

I also corrected SOLUTION.md: `make eval` requires a key on a fresh checkout. A green offline CI run does **not** verify live model extraction.

Latest submission commit: `3923619dce1787727543aa53992eef4130da136b`.
